George Ilenikhena marked his return from injury with a goal as Al-Ittihad defeated Pakhtakor 2-0 in the AFC Champions League in Jeddah on Tuesday. The Nigerian forward started the encounter at King Abdullah Sports City and opened the scoring shortly after the restart, reacting quickest to the rebound after an effort from the edge of the penalty area struck the woodwork. The strike marked a welcome return to action for the 19-year-old, who had been sidelined by injury shortly before the international break, thereby missing Nigeria’s double-header against Tanzania in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Ilenikhena was replaced with 17 minutes remaining, making way for former Sevilla striker Youssef En-Nesyri as Al-Ittihad sought to protect their advantage. The goal takes his tally to nine goals and three assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season Lampard sweats over Awoniyi’s ankle injury Ilenikhena maintains scoring form after Eagles omission Amedspor boss insists Orban not for sale The former Monaco striker will now hope to build on the performance and maintain his fitness as Al-Ittihad pursue domestic and continental honours.
